segments.text: Before coming to Yale, I worked in real estate investment funds, where I spent a lot of time evaluating development opportunities and building financial models. For my final project, I wanted to create something that could make that process more efficient. That's how TerraMind AI started.

TerraMind helps users evaluate different types of real estate investments, from residential developments to commercial and industrial properties. The process starts with the property's basic information, which the platform uses to guide the rest of the analysis.

One of the first steps is understanding what can actually be developed on a property. TerraMind can research development regulations, but it also allows users to provide their own information or upload documents, such as permits, contracts, or existing financial models, so the analysis can build on information they already have.

The platform then connects development assumptions, construction costs, projected revenues, and financing into a financial model. Instead of asking users to estimate the final returns, TerraMind calculates them from the underlying assumptions. Users can also export the model to Excel to review or continue working on it outside the application.
The feature I find most interesting is the chatbot. Instead of navigating through multiple spreadsheets, users can explain what they want to change in natural language.
Here, a ten percent increase in construction costs raises the hard cost from 24,000 to 26,400 pesos per square meter, and the equity IRR falls from 24.9% to 21.2%.
The assistant can update assumptions, incorporate more complex cash-flow schedules, and help users understand how those changes affect the investment.

I also wanted to make the platform easier to use, so I added speech-to-text functionality. Users can dictate instructions instead of typing them. And because I eventually want this to be useful in Mexico, the application supports both English and Spanish.

Another important objective was incorporating sustainability into investment decisions. TerraMind can help compare different improvements and evaluate their financial impact. The AI agents can also review the investment, identify risks, and suggest changes that could improve the project's performance.

I also wanted TerraMind to be useful beyond the initial investment decision. Users can save projects, return to their analyses, and monitor how investments are performing. The platform supports individual accounts to keep project information separate, as well as guest access for someone who just wants to explore it.

TerraMind is still a prototype, but it brings together several parts of real estate investing that are usually handled separately. I see it as a starting point for something I could continue developing after Yale, especially as I pursue my interest in real estate investment and sustainable development.
